absent: Numeric values of wait queue count, maximum single allocation size, page size and shift, default wake batch, and allocation orders.
Complete field layouts and sizes for queue, bitmap, wait state, waiter, scatter entry, table, append table, and iterator structures.
Internals of deferred clear, hint update, chain and marker helpers, allocation hint storage, and wait queue primitives owned elsewhere.
Shallow allocator policy, wake batch computation, and round robin allocation path not shown in these fragments.
Locking and sleeping context rules for table growth, page backing allocation, and diagnostic traversal under concurrency.
DMA address handling, cache maintenance scope beyond the single flush hook, and device memory mapping rules.
Error propagation for diagnostic output and for callers that observe truncated counts or empty results.

findings.text: Batch acquisition offers obtaining several tags that lie within one underlying word, starting search from a hint derived position and wrapping over all words. Round robin configuration disables this path and signals failure. On success it conveys which positions were claimed and the logical start offset and refreshes the allocation hint; on failure it signals with zero without changing caller offset.

Shallow acquisition delegates to the embedded bitmap shallow allocator with a caller supplied depth limit, warning when the limit is below the configured floor. A separate configuration operation records a new floor and recomputes wake batching from current depth.

Wakeup accounting accumulates completions and only triggers underlying queue wakeups once a configurable batch threshold is reached, using a separate wakeup counter to track already released batches. The internal wake pass rotates its starting queue for fairness and stops after satisfying the requested count. A distinct all wake operation bypasses batching and wakes every queue.

Release operations make tags reusable and account for wakeups. The batch variant clears several tags relative to a base, coalescing those sharing a word into one atomic update and skipping deferred handling. The single variant clears one position through deferred handling. Both order memory around the update, trigger wake accounting, and refresh the per cpu hint to the most recently freed position.

Waiter registration associates a waiter object with a queue and tracks how many waiters are active. Adding and preparing are idempotent with respect to association and only adjust the active count on first association; removal and finish detach and decrement only when associated. Preparation uses exclusive waiting semantics.

Diagnostic reporting renders queue state for inspection, covering the embedded bitmap summary, per cpu hint values across all possible processors, batching and index counters, active waiter count, per queue activity, round robin mode and shallow floor.

Counting helpers derive chain properties without modifying the list: total entries until termination, entries needed to cover a byte length with zero length needing none and insufficient coverage signaling invalid, scaled entry estimate for DMA lengths under a chunk size, and retrieval of the terminal entry with an expectation that it carries the end marker.
Initialization prepares scatter arrays by clearing storage and establishing chain markers, with a single entry convenience that also assigns a caller buffer and length.

Chained table management allocates enough linked chunks to hold a requested entry count, reserving a linking slot when a chunk is full, chaining pieces together, marking the final entry, and recording both usable and allocated counts. Freeing walks the chain and releases each piece through a supplied releaser, supporting an externally owned first chunk, and clears the table head. Simple wrappers use a standard maximum chunk size and clean up on failure.

Page based construction merges physically contiguous pages into segments bounded by a page aligned maximum, supporting incremental appends that may extend the previous tail when contiguous. It precomputes how many segments are needed, grows the chain as required, assigns page offset and length per segment, updates usable counts, marks termination when no further pages are expected, and restores the prior tail length if growth fails.

Order based lists allocate both the list storage and the backing pages of a given allocation order to cover a byte length, rounding coverage up and optionally reserving an extra slot for future chaining. Page allocation failure releases all previously acquired pages and the list. Complementary releases free backing pages for a bounded or unbounded prefix and then the list, with order zero conveniences for common use.

Page iteration abstracts traversal across entries that may span multiple pages. Initialization records the list head, remaining entry budget and starting page offset with no initial advance. Advancement moves within the current entry or across entries until a valid page is found, exhausting when the budget ends or the chain terminates. A DMA variant counts pages from DMA length rather than CPU length.

Mapping iteration layers page traversal with per page mapping lifecycle. Startup clears state, begins page traversal and records direction and mapping mode. Page acquisition derives the valid byte window within the current page. Skipping discards any active mapping and consumes a byte distance across pages, reporting whether the distance was fully satisfied. Stopping accounts consumed bytes, flushes on writeback direction, unmaps according to atomic or local or general mode, and clears mapping state.

Round robin mode disables batch acquisition and per cpu hint updates, while non round robin mode only records hints for tags within current depth. Hint state is consulted before acquisition and refreshed after acquisition or release, providing locality without affecting correctness.

Wakeups are suppressed entirely when no waiters are active. Otherwise completions accumulate separately from released wakeups, and a new wake pass occurs only when unreleased completions reach the batch size, preserving at most batch granularity. Wake passes advance the start index before inspecting each queue so successive passes rotate fairly even when queues remain non empty.

A tag in use always has its clear indication unset; setting that indication permits immediate reuse, so release orders prior accesses before the atomic clear and orders the clear before waiter observation. The single release pairs with allocation side ordering and with waiter sleep ordering to avoid lost wakeups.

Active waiter count equals the number of waiter objects currently associated with the queue. Association is established once per waiter and cleared on detachment, preventing double counting when the same waiter is added or prepared repeatedly or finished without association.

Scatter chains use explicit end marking on the final usable entry and, when spanning chunks, reserve the last slot of each non terminal chunk for linkage rather than data. Usable and allocated counts reflect this reservation, and freeing accounts for the reserved slots when walking the chain.

Scatter chunk allocation selects a single page allocator path exactly when the requested chunk size equals the maximum single allocation threshold, with leak tracking paired between allocation and release; all other sizes use the general object allocator and its matching release.

Segment merging requires both consecutive physical page numbers and compatible device memory association, and never extends a segment beyond the page aligned maximum. Continuation appends require zero initial offset and are unsupported on configurations without chaining.

Page counts are derived by rounding offset plus length up to page granularity. Mapping iteration never exposes more than one page window at a time, tracks remaining bytes within that window separately from consumed bytes within the active mapping, and requires consumed not to exceed exposed length.

Bitmap word claims, completion and wakeup counters, active waiter count and wake position are mutated with atomic primitives and read with once semantics, without sleeping locks in these fragments. Word claims retry compare exchange until success; wakeup release uses compare exchange on the wakeup counter; batch releases coalesce into single atomic clear per word.

Memory ordering around release and wake observation relies on explicit barriers: before atomic to order prior data accesses ahead of reuse, after atomic to order the clear ahead of waiter state checks, plus a full barrier before unconditional wake all. Per cpu hint stores are explicitly marked as racy and carry no ordering guarantees.

The queue object observed here couples an embedded bitmap with wake batching state, a rotating wake position, active waiter and completion counters, an array of wait states, per cpu allocation hints, a round robin selector and a shallow floor. The bitmap contributes depth, word array with count and shift, and round robin mode; wait state contributes a wait queue head; waiter contributes association back pointer and queue entry.

Table objects couple a head pointer with usable and original entry counts; append tables add a running total allocation count and a tail pointer for incremental growth. Entries carry page linkage, offset and length plus DMA length, with chain and end markers managed separately from payload.

Page iterators couple current entry pointer, page offset within that entry, remaining entry budget and a pending advance. Mapping iterators layer on top a current page and mapped address, total exposed length and consumed prefix, byte offset and remaining window within the page, and direction plus mapping mode flags.

Waiter objects move between unassociated and associated with a specific queue. Add and prepare transition from unassociated to associated while incrementing activity; delete and finish transition back while decrementing. Repeated add or prepare while associated leaves association unchanged; delete or finish while unassociated only detaches queue linkage without counter change.

Mapping state cycles between idle with no active address and mapped with a valid address page length and consumed prefix. Advancing or skipping from idle acquires a new page window; stopping from mapped releases resources and returns to idle. Skipping from mapped first stops then consumes distance; over consumption is treated as a programming error.

Append construction progresses from empty with no head, to headed with allocated chunks and a tail, to terminated with end marking once no further pages are expected. Growth requests that land on a chain reservation allocate and link a new chunk; allocation failure leaves prior tail length restored and termination unmarked.

Queue subsystem entry points callable from outside this file are the batch claim, shallow claim, shallow floor setter, single and batch release, batched and unconditional wake, diagnostic show, and waiter add delete prepare finish operations.

Scatter subsystem entry points are the counting and terminal helpers, table initialization, chained allocation and release, page based append and segment construction, order based list allocation and release, page iterator start and advance including DMA advance, and mapping iterator start skip and stop operations.

Growth and page backing paths validate sizes and handle exhaustion: zero length tables and oversize no chain requests are rejected, integer overflow in element count and chain reservation yields empty result without allocation, page allocation failure unwinds prior pages and list storage, and append growth failure restores prior tail length.

Programming error checks warn on shallow depth below floor, missing mapping direction, consumed beyond exposed length, atomic mapping without disabled faults, length left after list build, and mismatched total versus usable counts; terminal retrieval asserts end marking. These indicate caller contract violations rather than runtime failures.

Reuse races are hazardous if release ordering is weakened: a tag whose clear indication is set may be immediately reallocated, so prior data accesses must be ordered before the clear and the clear before waiter checks. Waker and waiter barrier pairing prevents missed wakeups between queue activity tests and sleep preparation.

Two sizing constants shape behavior as facts: SBQ_WAIT_QUEUES defines wake rotation fan out and diagnostic iteration bound, and SG_MAX_SINGLE_ALLOC selects between page based and general object based chunk storage and defines chunking granularity.

Page granularity facts govern merging and counting: PAGE_SIZE defines segment alignment and per page window limits, PAGE_SHIFT defines index scaling, and page frame contiguity defines mergeability. Distinct failure signals EINVAL and ENOMEM and EOPNOTSUPP convey invalid argument and exhausted memory and unsupported operation for table sizing and allocation and no chain continuation cases.

Mapping direction and mode flags are ABI facts: SG_MITER_TO_SG and SG_MITER_FROM_SG request writeback versus read, plus SG_MITER_ATOMIC and SG_MITER_LOCAL select unmap path and fault handling expectations. At least one direction bit is required at startup.
